headline: Van den Bergh's Tour Card loss blamed on injuries and lost confidence
standfirst: Belgian analyst Rudy Lanssens says the former world number five should consider a break from competing as he rebuilds.
body: Dimitri Van den Bergh has lost his PDC Tour Card, according to Dartsnews, ending the guaranteed place on the professional circuit that he held through his years among the sport's leading players. The 32-year-old Belgian now faces a period of rebuilding.

The assessment that has drawn attention comes from Rudy Lanssens, a darts analyst for the Belgian broadcaster VTM. Speaking to the newspaper HLN, he described Van den Bergh's decline as "a cocktail of factors" rather than the result of one single problem.

Lanssens pointed to recent injuries and difficulties in the player's private life. He also said the heavy criticism of Van den Bergh's theatrical walk-on had worn on him, and that the player had eventually tired of it himself. In his view, each setback made the next poor result more likely.

He does not believe the underlying ability has gone. Lanssens argued that the technique and smooth throw that carried Van den Bergh to the top are intact, and that the problem is largely psychological. He called darts a sport that is about 80 per cent mental and said worries make it hard to perform, which in turn erodes confidence and results.

The analyst recalled a player who was consistently ranked in the top five and acted as an ambassador for the PDC. Van den Bergh's walk-on, set to Pharrell Williams' "Happy", made him a favourite with crowds, and Lanssens credited him with helping to broaden the audience for darts in Belgium, where VTM 2 has broadcast the sport.

Lanssens fears that simply playing more matches would do little for Van den Bergh at present, and he suggests a break from the sport. A related Dartsnews headline refers to the Tour Card being lost after the World Championship, so the exact timing of the change is unclear from the sources.
